title.narrative: Poverty Alleviation, Comprehensive, Inclusive and Adaptive Social Protection

description.narrative: The Poverty Alleviation, Comprehensive, Inclusive and Adaptive Social Protection (PROAKTIF) initiative is Australia’s main avenue of direct support for social protection and poverty alleviation in Indonesia. PROAKTIF is a continuation of Australia’s longstanding partnership with Indonesia since 2011. PROAKTIF consists of a policy think-tank (formerly known as the National Poverty Alleviation and Acceleration Team - TNP2K), that provides evidence-based policy advice, program implementation support, and cross-ministry coordination on social protection and poverty reduction efforts.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Australia supported the National Team for the Acceleration of Poverty Reduction policy think tank (TNP2K) to continue to provide evidence-based policy advice to Indonesia to reform and improve social assistance programs that reached 150 million people, including over 12 million people with disabilities. In 2023 TNP2K undertook monitoring and evaluation of programs jointly with government, generating evidence to contribute to improvements in program design and implementation. TNP2K contributed modelling and policy advice to inform Indonesia’s use of targeted special payments through the largest national program (Sembako) to mitigate the impact of ElNino on poor and vulnerable households. TNP2K also contributed to the improvement of household level data available to the Ministry of Social Affairs that is used to reach social assistance program recipients. This builds on TNP2K’s longstanding support to the Ministry of Social Affairs to improve the quality and effectiveness of social assistance programs, including the reform of Sembako.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia, through the National Team for the Acceleration Poverty Reduction (TNP2K) Policy Think tank, is supporting Indonesia’s efforts to reform energy subsidies. In 2023 TNP2K continued to provide evidence-based advice on implementation models that would improve the targeting of subsidies to the poorest households. For electricity subsidy reform, TNP2K worked with the state-owned electricity provider, the Bureau of Statistics, and the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources to cross-check subsidy recipients against government household level databases of poor and vulnerable families – ie. the Extreme Poverty Targeting database which was developed by TNP2K with government partners, and the Ministry of Social Affairs’ database. This identified 866,000 poor and extreme poor households for inclusion in the subsidy. ‍ In preparation for potential Liquid Petroleum Gas (LPG) subsidy reform, TNP2K supported the National Energy Company to do modelling to for a targeted subsidy where only eligible poor households can purchase subsidised 3kg LPG.

Australia, through the National Team for the Acceleration of Poverty Reduction (TNP2K) Policy Think tank, supported the development of foundational systems and regulations to support the implementation of Presidential Instruction Number 4 of 2022 which sets out Indonesia’s goal of eliminating extreme poverty by 2024 (EPRI). The database used to improve the targeting of Indonesia’s efforts to households living in extreme poverty was developed by TNP2K with government partners. Indonesia formally mandated use of the database in Ministerial Decree No 30 of 2022 (Human Development and Cultural Affairs). In 2023, TNP2K led an update of the database to further improve the targeting of Indonesia’s extreme poverty reduction efforts. 1.7 million families that were previously excluded were added, increasing the database to 71 million households. The database is used by government at national and subnational level to target their extreme poverty reduction efforts – in 2023, 473 agencies accessed the data.

Australia, through the PROAKTIF program, continues the longstanding support to the Policy Support Team (former TNP2K Policy Team). They provide evidence-based policy advice to reform and improve Indonesia’s social protection programs that reach more than 150 million poor and vulnerable people across Indonesia. ‍ In 2024 the Policy Support Team evaluated social protection programs, including the Government Food Reserves (Cadangan Pangan Pemerintah-CPP) – a shock-responsive social protection program, which reached 22 million vulnerable households. The Policy Team assessed the program’s targeting accuracy and beneficiary experiences. The findings showed improved targeting: 85% of recipients were from the poorest 40% of the population (up from 31% in 2023). A further 52% were newly identified using the extreme poverty targeting database (P3KE), which was operationalised by the Policy Support Team. Following affirmative targeting, the proportion of single elderly beneficiaries increased from 23% to 42%. ‍ The final monitoring report was presented to key government officials and contributed to discussions during a limited cabinet meeting. The CPP program was later extended with additional distribution until the end of 2024 to help address ongoing El Niño impacts and rising pockets of extreme poverty.

Australia, through the Policy Support Team (former TNP2K Policy Team) supported the development and operationalisation of the extreme poverty targeting database (P3KE). They support the implementation of Presidential Regulation No 4/2022, which sets out Indonesia’s goal of eliminating extreme poverty by 2024. P3KE is used by national and local governments to improve the targeting of their extreme poverty programs. ‍ In 2024, 364 national and local government agencies accessed P3KE data. An example of how this is used at the local government level is the city of Tebing Tinggi. Following the operationalisation of the P3KE database, this local government issued a mayoral decree to formally adopt P3KE as the official data source for extreme poverty targeting. The city used the database to deliver a wide range of services to poor and vulnerable households, including rice assistance for over 12,900 recipients, stunting prevention programs, vocational training, as well as housing and sanitation interventions. P3KE data was integrated into the city’s planning documents which ensured alignment between planning and local poverty programming.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia, through the Policy Support Team (former TNP2K Policy Team), supported Indonesia’s goal of eliminating extreme poverty by 2024. Working in close collaboration with key government partners, the Policy Support Team contributed to issuing fiscal incentive regulations to reward local governments whose budgets align with national poverty reduction strategies. The Policy Support Team provided technical support on the development and operationalisation of the extreme poverty budget tagging mechanism to assess local governments’ performance on planning and budgeting. Budget tagging was used to assess to local budget allocations and formed one of the three indicators for awarding incentive. ‍ In 2024, Ministry of Finance awarded IDR 775 billion (AUD 75 million) in fiscal incentives to 9 provinces, 99 districts, and 22 cities. The incentive has helped direct additional resources to regions most in need of support. For example, 66% of the provinces and districts that received fiscal incentives in 2024 had low to moderate fiscal capacity.
